excerpt: WorkClaw gives teams AI coworkers built on OpenClaw that work in Slack and Teams, each with a role, manager and cloud computer. Team plan $29/month.
content:
WorkClaw lets a company hire AI coworkers, which it calls Workmates or Claws, that sit in Slack or Microsoft Teams next to the rest of the team. Each one has a job title, a manager in your org chart and its own cloud-hosted computer, and can reach more than 3,000 apps. Every workspace starts with a Team Assistant for questions, meeting summaries and reminders; you can then add ready-made roles such as a scheduling assistant, software engineer, outbound sales researcher, research analyst, recruiter, content marketer or data analyst, or build your own by chatting. Skills can be installed from a library or created and shared across the team.

WorkClaw is built on the open-source OpenClaw agent and adds controls on top: admins decide access, app connections and which skills can be installed, and credentials sit in a vault. The company says it is SOC 2 compliant. It is made by Workmate (Workmate Labs), whose privacy policy gives an address in Dover, Delaware.

Pricing is based on usage rather than seats. The Team plan is $29 a month with 30,000 credits, shared across unlimited users, and new teams get $100 of free credits without a card. Credits pay both for each Workmate's cloud computer (from 750 credits a day) and for AI usage. WorkClaw was founded by Will Ruben, whose Product Hunt headline lists past roles at Instagram, Facebook and Coinbase. It launched on Product Hunt on 20 June 2026, hunted by Rohan Chaubey, and finished #1 for the day with 352 upvotes and 89 comments.

We have not tested WorkClaw ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page, blog and privacy policy, its Product Hunt page and the official pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Slack and Microsoft Teams, with a web dashboard
profile.starts_at: Team $29/month (30,000 credits); $100 free credits to start
profile.summary_short: AI coworkers built on OpenClaw that work in Slack and Teams with their own cloud computer
use_cases: A shared team assistant that answers questions from your docs and summarises meetings
A scheduling Workmate with its own email address that books meetings within your rules
Codebase Q&A, ticket drafts and PR summaries for an engineering team
Prospect research and outreach drafts for sales
Recurring reports and metric summaries from spreadsheets and dashboards

fit: work in Slack or Teams and want AI agents the whole team can use
like the idea of OpenClaw but want admin controls and hosting handled
prefer usage-based pricing to per-seat pricing
not_fit: need a predictable flat bill: always-on Workmates use credits every day
want to bring your own model key on the entry plan: that is a Business-plan feature

pricing.intro: WorkClaw prices by credits, not seats. Prices are from workclaw.com, in US dollars.

plans.name: Team
plans.detail: 30,000 credits a month shared across unlimited users, plus $100 of free credits per team; unlimited Workmates, pre-built and custom skills, Claude model access, 100+ integrations. 14-day free trial, no card

plans.name: Business
plans.detail: Volume discounts, bring your own API key, dedicated infrastructure, DPA and SOC 2 reports, SLA, SSO, audit logs and role-based limits

notes: Top-ups: 20,000 credits for $20 at any time. Roughly $1 = 1,000 credits at the entry tier.
Each Workmate's cloud computer costs from 750 credits a day; Workmates can be paused.
Credits reset monthly on the Team plan. If you run out, Workmates pause until you top up.

alternatives.intro: Other ways to build AI agents that work for a team. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Lindy
items.what: AI assistant and agent builder for email, meetings and workflows
items.starts_at: Free with $50 of credits for 7 days; Team from $49.99/month per user
items.difference: Bills every active user; WorkClaw has no per-seat price.

items.name: Relevance AI
items.what: Platform for building teams of AI agents for sales, support and operations
items.difference: A builder platform with its own interface; WorkClaw's agents live inside Slack and Teams with their own computer.

pros: No per-seat pricing; invite the whole team
$100 of free credits and a 14-day trial without a card
Ready-made roles plus custom skills you can share
Admin controls and a credential vault on top of OpenClaw
Workmates pause instead of overspending when credits run out
cons: Always-on Workmates cost credits daily, so bills scale with how many you run
Credits do not roll over on the Team plan
Bring-your-own-key and SSO are Business-plan only

posts.author: arc.
posts.note: notes that you onboard WorkClaw like a person: title, manager, laptop and tool access, then repeat to build a team in Slack or Teams.

quotes.text: I'd want to know what the approval and rollback model looks like for actions that touch money or customers
quotes.reply: Each app is connected to each Claw separately, and you choose whether a Claw is proactive or only answers when spoken to, and which channels it listens in.
quotes.author: Jibran Ahmed

quotes.text: If I create 10 Claws, who is responsible when something goes wrong?
quotes.reply: Many customers set up specialised Claws plus one orchestrator Claw that combines their outputs and reports to a person; the human decides the org chart.
quotes.author: Moh

faq.a: A service for hiring AI coworkers (Workmates) that work in Slack or Microsoft Teams. Each has a role, a manager, its own cloud computer and access to thousands of apps, and they are built on the open-source OpenClaw agent.
The Team plan is $29 a month for 30,000 credits shared across unlimited users, with $100 of free credits to start. Extra credits are $20 per 20,000. Business plans are custom.
Both keeping a Workmate's cloud computer running (from 750 credits a day) and the AI work it does. Workmates can be paused when not needed.

faq.q: What happens if I run out of credits?
faq.a: Workmates pause automatically with their context intact and resume after you top up or upgrade. There is no overdraft.

faq.q: Is it secure enough for a company?
faq.a: WorkClaw says it is SOC 2 compliant, stores credentials in a vault, and lets admins control access, integrations and skill installs. Business plans add SSO, audit logs and dedicated infrastructure.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to WorkClaw?
faq.a: Lindy, an AI assistant and agent builder billed per user, or Relevance AI, a platform for building agent teams.

liked: Focus on real team workflows rather than one person chatting with one assistant
Agents that feel like part of the team in Slack
asked: Who is accountable when several Claws hand work to each other (teams often add an orchestrator Claw that reports to a person)
What stops a proactive Claw doing the wrong thing across thousands of apps (apps are connected per Claw, and you choose whether it is proactive and which channels it listens in)
How two Claws avoid clashing on the same task (each runs in its own VM and they coordinate by chat)
What people automate first (research, analysis, marketing, email triage and project management)
criticised: A commenter warned that proactive agents can 'do the wrong thing at scale' and asked about approvals and rollback for actions touching money or customers

quotes.text: one that acts on its own across 3,000 apps can do the wrong thing at scale before anyone notices.
quotes.author: Jibran Ahmed

quotes.text: The challenge with AI teammates isn’t creating them, it’s managing them.
